prompt: A pharmacist tests a drug at three doses (low, medium, high) given at two times of day (morning, evening). Every combination is tested. How many treatments does this experiment have?
hint: A treatment is one specific combination of a level from each factor. How many factors are there, and how many levels does each have?

hints.text: A treatment is one specific combination of a level from each factor. How many factors are there, and how many levels does each have?
Dose has three levels and time of day has two. Every dose is paired with every time, so multiply the number of levels.

explanation: There are two factors: dose (3 levels) and time of day (2 levels).
Each treatment pairs one dose with one time, and every pairing is used.
$3 \times 2 = 6$ treatments: low-morning, low-evening, medium-morning, medium-evening, high-morning, high-evening.

alternativeExplanations.title: Make a grid
steps: Rows: low, medium, high. Columns: morning, evening.
The grid has $3 \times 2 = 6$ cells, and each cell is one treatment.
